mainTopic: The parts of the מזבח that are required for it to be valid, and the שיתין (drainpipes under the מזבח): where they came from, how deep they go, and what was found in them
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא listing the parts every מזבח must have: a כבש (ramp), a קרן (horn), a יסוד (base), and a square shape. If any one of them is missing, the מזבח is פסול for עבודה. רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds that the סובב (ledge) is also required. The גמרא then turns to the שיתין, the pits under the מזבח that received the wine of the נסכים. רבי יוחנן teaches from a פסוק in שיר השירים that ה׳ created the שיתין during the six days of creation. דבי רבי ישמעאל reads בראשית as ברא שית, 'He created the pit.' רבי יוסי learns from the vineyard song in ישעיהו that the שיתין are hollow and reach down to the תהום. Finally, רבי אלעזר בר צדוק describes a small gap near the כבש: once every seventy years, young כהנים gathered hardened wine from there and burned it בקדושה. The פסוק for that practice is quoted, and its explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An altar missing its essential parts is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ending of a ברייתא: a מזבח without a כבש, קרן, יסוד, or square shape is פסול for עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any altar that is missing a ramp, a horn, a base, or a square shape is disqualified for the Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא that the גמרא is quoting. This ברייתא lists the parts a מזבח must have to be usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four features are essential: the ramp to walk up, the horns at the corners, the base at the bottom, and a square outline. If any one of them is missing, the whole מזבח becomes פסול for עבודה. The יסוד is on this list, which matters for the surrounding discussion about the bottom of the מזבח and the pipes beneath it.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש
The ramp leading up to the altar
A horn, one of the raised corners of the altar
The base at the bottom of the altar

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The word שֶׁכׇּל ('for any') connects back to an argument from the previous part of the daf. This is not a brand-new topic.

phrases.english: for any altar that does not have
not a ramp and not a horn
and not a base and not a square shape
is disqualified for the service.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the list of the essential parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that was quoted on the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזבח lacking a כבש, קרן, יסוד, or square shape is פסול for עבודה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds the ledge
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says that a missing סובב also makes the מזבח פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: even the surrounding ledge is required.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא adds one more item to the list of essential parts of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion listed four required parts. רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that the סובב, the ledge running around the middle of the מזבח, is also required. In his view, a מזבח without it is also פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The ledge that runs around the middle of the altar

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
even the surrounding ledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַסּוֹבֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the list in Step 1. It is an expansion, not a disagreement over the four items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סובב is also essential, and without it the מזבח is פסול.

steps.title: The drainpipes were created during the six days of creation
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: the שיתין were created in the six days of creation, as hinted in שיר השירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the drainpipes under the altar were created during the six days of creation, as the verse says: 'The hidden parts of your thighs are like links of a chain, the work of a craftsman's hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: the שיתין under the מזבח. It brings רבי יוחנן's teaching that they go back to the creation of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שיתין are the pits or pipes under the מזבח where the wine of the נסכים drained down. רבי יוחנן says they were not made by human builders. ה׳ made them during the six days of creation, and he brings a פסוק as his source. The next step explains how that פסוק is being read.

keyTerms.meaning: The drainpipes or pits beneath the altar that received the poured wine

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
the drainpipes were created from the six days of creation,
as it is said: 'The hidden parts of your thighs'
'are like links of a chain, the work of a craftsman's hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the parts of the מזבח to the pipes beneath it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיתין were created during the six days of creation.

steps.title: Reading the verse word by word
steps.stepSummary: Each part of the פסוק is matched to the שיתין: hidden, hollow and deep, and made by ה׳ Himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The hidden parts of your thighs' — these are the drainpipes. 'Like links of a chain' — they are hollow and go down to the depths. 'The work of a craftsman's hands' — this is the handiwork of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves רבי יוחנן's teaching by reading it phrase by phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'hidden' fits the pipes because they are concealed inside and under the מזבח. The word חלאים sounds like מחוללין ('hollow'), which teaches that the pipes are hollow and reach down to the תהום. The 'craftsman' is הקב״ה, and that is what proves the pipes were created by ה׳ at the time of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The hidden curves of your thighs
Links of a chain (here read as hollow)
The deep abyss beneath the earth

phrases.english: 'The hidden parts of your thighs' — these are the drainpipes.
'Like links of a chain' — for they are hollow and go down to the depths.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: חלאים (links) sounds like מחוללין (hollow).

phrases.english: 'The work of a craftsman's hands' —
this is the work of the craftsmanship
of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in Step 3 supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that ה׳ created the שיתין during creation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים ז:ב, read phrase by phrase.

steps.title: Reading בראשית as ברא שית, 'He created the pit'
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל reads the Torah's first word, בראשית, as ברא שית ('He created the pit').
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'In the beginning' — do not read it as בראשית but as ברא שית, 'He created the pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second source is brought to support the idea that the שיתין date back to creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method used here is called אל תיקרי: the word is read in a new way to draw out a hidden lesson. בראשית is split into ברא ('He created') and שית ('pit'). This hints that the pit under the מזבח was part of creation from the very first word of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Do not read it as (a way of drawing a lesson from a different reading)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תיקרי does not change the actual text of the Torah. The word still says בראשית. It only adds an extra layer of meaning.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
'In the beginning' — do not read 'Bereshit,'
but rather 'Bara shit' — 'He created a pit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the same idea as Steps 3–4.
steps.raayaObject: That the שיתין were created at the beginning of creation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first word of בראשית, read as ברא שית.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the pipes reach down to the deep, from ישעיהו's song of the vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that the שיתין are hollow and go down to the תהום, and he brings the פסוקים of the vineyard song in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי says: the drainpipes are hollow and go down to the depths, as it says: 'Let me sing for my beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill. He dug it, cleared it of stones, planted it with choice vines, built a tower in it, and also carved out a wine vat in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי יוסי's teaching about how deep the שיתין go. Here it quotes the full פסוק, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes the same point about depth that was drawn from חלאים in Step 4, but from a different פסוק. He uses the parable of ה׳'s vineyard in ישעיהו. This step only lays out the verse; the matching of each part to the מקדש comes next.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
the drainpipes are hollow and go down to the depths,
as it is said: 'Let me sing for my beloved'
'a song of my beloved about his vineyard.'

phrases.aramaic: כֶּרֶם הָיָה לִידִידִי בְּקֶרֶן בֶּן שָׁמֶן.
phrases.english: 'My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill.'
'He dug it and cleared it of stones,'
'and planted it with choice vines,'
'and built a tower in its midst,'
'and also carved out a wine vat in it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source teaching that the שיתין reach the תהום, the same idea drawn from חלאים in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיתין are hollow and go down to the תהום.

steps.title: Mapping the vineyard onto the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The vine is the בית המקדש, the tower is the מזבח, and the carved-out vat is the שיתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He planted it with choice vines' — this is the Temple. 'He built a tower in its midst' — this is the altar. 'And also carved out a wine vat in it' — these are the drainpipes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי explains how each part of the vineyard parable stands for a part of the מקדש. This is the proof for his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vat in a vineyard is a deep pit carved into rock that collects wine, just as the שיתין collect the wine of the נסכים. The verb חצב ('carved out') points to a deep hollow. Since the owner of the vineyard is ה׳, it was He who carved it.
steps.whatToRemember: Three sources (רבי יוחנן, דבי רבי ישמעאל, and רבי יוסי) all teach the same thing: the שיתין under the מזבח are deep, hollow pits made by ה׳, not ordinary man-made pipes.

phrases.english: 'And planted it with choice vines' — this is the Temple;
'and built a tower in its midst' — this is the altar;
'and also carved out a wine vat in it' — these are the drainpipes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the פסוק quoted in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the שיתין are deep pits made by ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו ה:ב: the wine vat carved in the vineyard.

steps.title: Once every seventy years, the hardened wine was gathered and burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק describes a small gap near the כבש. Every seventy years young כהנים collected hardened wine from it and burned it בקדושה, and the פסוק for this begins at the end of the amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said: there was a small gap between the ramp and the altar, on the west side of the ramp. Once every seventy years, young priests would go down there and gather hardened wine that looked like round cakes of pressed figs. They would come and burn it in a holy place, as it says: 'In holiness pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳' —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing what happened to the leftover wine of the נסכים over many years. This passage ends just as the פסוק source is being quoted, and its explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine poured on the מזבח drained down and, over decades, hardened into lumps like fig cakes. Even though it had dried up, it was still holy. So the young כהנים burned it inside the קדושה of the מקדש rather than throwing it away. The פסוק 'בקדש הסך' is brought to show that the wine must be treated with holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: In a state or place of holiness
A wine libation poured on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished. The dash after the פסוק means the גמרא is about to explain how this verse proves the burning. That explanation comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: לוּל קָטָן הָיָה בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: there was a small gap between the ramp and the altar
on the west side of the ramp,
and once every seventy years
young priests would go down there,
and gather from there hardened wine
that looked like round cakes of pressed figs,
and they would come and burn it in holiness,
as it is said: 'In holiness pour'
'a libation of strong drink to ה׳' —
phrases.notes: במדבר כח:ז. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the wine that drains under the מזבח, now focusing on what was done with the leftover wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hardened wine from the נסכים was collected every seventy years and burned בקדושה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that wine from the נסכים keeps its holiness even after decades, so it must be disposed of in a holy way.
